stories.summary: The Africa CDC has warned it will blacklist organisations that fail to provide transparency and accountability for funds received for disease outbreak resp

stories.title: Ebola: FG orders 46 exposed persons on 21-day no-fly list
stories.summary: The Federal Government has ordered 46 persons who had contact with an Ebola patient in Nigeria to be placed on a 21-day no-fly list to contain the virus.

stories.title: Ebola: Medical expert demands contact tracing for all travellers, no VIP exemptions
stories.summary: A medical expert, Prof Oladapo Ashiru, has called for mandatory Ebola contact tracing for all travellers in Nigeria, with no VIP exemptions at airports.

stories.title: Ebola: No cause for panic yet, experts tell Nigerians
stories.summary: Nigerians have been warned against panicking following the first confirmed case of Ebola virus, with experts saying more efforts should be geared towards

stories.title: Ebola: Anambra monitors seven persons of interest
stories.summary: The Anambra State government says its Epidemiology Unit is monitoring seven persons of interest following a reported Ebola case in Abuja.

stories.title: Ebola: Firm urges vigilance, warns against misinformation
stories.summary: SUNU Health Nigeria has urged vigilance following the confirmation of an Ebola case in the FCT, advising citizens to follow preventive measures.

stories.title: (PHOTOS) Ebola: NCDC convenes emergency meeting, finalises incident action plan
stories.summary: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention has convened an emergency meeting to finalise its incident action plan for the Ebola outbreak in Nige

stories.title: NAFDAC raids Lagos factory producing bitters with cough syrup registration number
stories.summary: NAFDAC has uncovered an illegal factory in Agege, Lagos, producing herbal bitters using a registration number belonging to a cough syrup.

stories.title: Ebola: Senate seeks emergency funds, mandatory border screening
stories.summary: The Nigerian Senate has urged the FG to release emergency funds and introduce mandatory health screening at all borders to curb the spread of Ebola.

stories.title: Ebola: Ogun steps up surveillance, traces 111 travellers after Abuja case
stories.summary: Ogun State has intensified Ebola surveillance and traced 111 travellers after a case was announced in Abuja, the state's health commissioner has said.

stories.title: Ebola: How Nigerians can prevent infection
stories.summary: The Federal Government has confirmed an Ebola case in Abuja. Learn how the virus spreads, its symptoms, and the precautions Nigerians can take to prevent i

stories.title: Ebola: Uganda seeks Nigerian woman’s travel history from FG
stories.summary: Uganda's Ministry of Health is seeking travel details from Nigeria after a woman who transited through the country tested positive for Ebola in the FCT.

stories.title: NHIA boosts fee-for-service payments to hospitals by 373%
stories.summary: The National Health Insurance Authority has increased reimbursements to healthcare providers under its fee-for-service arrangement by 373 per cent as part

stories.title: Foreign veterinary team examines ailing African elephant in Pakistan
stories.summary: They say Madhubalu, who lives in a Safari Park in Karachi, has improved somewhat but time will tell if all will be well.

stories.title: Declare state of emergency on substance abuse, mental health expert urges govt
stories.summary: A consultant psychiatrist has urged the government to declare a state of emergency on substance abuse, warning it is worsening Nigeria's mental health cris

stories.title: WHO releases new guidance to prevent heat-related illness at mass gatherings
stories.summary: The World Health Organisation has released new guidance to help governments and event organisers prevent and manage heat-related illnesses at mass gatherin

stories.title: Nigeria vaccinates 18 million girls against cervical cancer
stories.summary: The Nigerian government has vaccinated over 18 million adolescent girls against HPV, covering 76% of its target to eliminate cervical cancer.

stories.title: Wash dog bite for 15 minutes to prevent rabies, vet advises
stories.summary: A veterinary expert advises washing a dog bite with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes to prevent rabies before seeking medical attention.

stories.title: Bahrain says Iranian attack hit industrial facility and caused a fire
stories.summary: Bahrain's Interior Ministry said an Iranian attack struck a civilian industrial facility on Saturday, causing a fire and material damage but no injuries. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted US military positions in the kingdom, home to the US Navy's Fifth Fleet. Civil Defence teams worked to contain the blaze.

stories.title: Brazil's Bolsonaro in intensive care with acute bowel obstruction
stories.summary: Former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro was admitted to the intensive care unit at DF Star hospital in Brasilia with an acute obstructive abdomen after being hospitalised with severe abdominal pain. The hospital said the 71-year-old was clinically stable, conscious and breathing on his own, with a gastric tube inserted and no expected discharge date. He has had repeated abdominal problems since being stabbed on the campaign trail in 2018.

stories.title: Thousands march in Lisbon as living costs and rents fuel anger
stories.summary: Thousands of people marched through central Lisbon in heavy rain to protest against soaring living costs, a deepening housing crisis and low wages. Organiser CGTP, Portugal's largest trade union federation, demanded higher wages and pensions, lower prices for essentials and measures to curb housing costs. House prices have more than doubled since 2017 and rents for new leases have nearly doubled.

stories.title: Uganda cancels Standard Gauge Railway contract with Turkish firm Yapi Merkezi
stories.summary: Uganda's Chief of Defence Forces, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, announced the Standard Gauge Railway contract with Turkish construction firm Yapi Merkezi has been cancelled indefinitely, saying a more suitable partner would be found. The deal covered a 270-kilometre line from Malaba on the Kenyan border to Kampala. The project had already been delayed by difficulties securing financing.

stories.title: Somalia and EU hold Brussels security talks ahead of AUSSOM mandate decision
stories.summary: Somalia and the European Union convened security transition talks in Brussels with AUSSOM troop-contributing countries Djibouti, Ethiopia, Kenya and Uganda, alongside the US, UK, Turkiye, Egypt and Gulf states. Participants stressed close coordination as the African Union mission's UN authorisation runs to 31 December 2026. The Security Council is expected to consider renewal next month.

stories.title: Kenya braces for intensifying November rains as forecasters warn of floods
stories.summary: Kenya's meteorological services forecast above-average rainfall in more than 40 counties including Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu and Garissa through November. The outlook warns that excessive rain could expose vulnerable communities to flooding, infrastructure damage and disruption to livelihoods. Rainfall remains critical to agriculture, livestock and water security.

stories.title: Tinubu holds low-key Ibadan rally after Bayelsa boat tragedy
stories.summary: President Bola Tinubu and First Lady Oluremi Tinubu arrived in Ibadan for the South-West leg of the APC presidential campaign at Mapo Hall, the seventh stop of the 2027 re-election tour. Tinubu directed the rally be observed without much fanfare in honour of those lost in the Bayelsa boat disaster. He later flew to Lagos, where he was received by Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu.

stories.title: NAFDAC destroys ₦100bn of fake, expired and banned products in Ogun
stories.summary: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control destroyed falsified, expired, banned and substandard products valued at about ₦100 billion at Ogwama Dumpsite in Ogere Remo, Ogun State. The haul included unregistered medicines, banned Analgin injections, expired codeine syrups, counterfeit cosmetics and unwholesome food. Director-General Mojisola Adeyeye said the aim was to stop dangerous products re-entering the market.

stories.title: S&P 500 and Dow close in correction as AI rout deepens
stories.summary: The S&P 500 fell 3.7% and the Dow dropped about 950 points, both entering correction territory, while the Nasdaq tumbled 5.3% to erase its 2026 gains. Nvidia slid roughly 12% and finished the week down 23%, its worst week since the financial crisis, and Anthropic gave back most of its IPO-day pop. For the week the S&P lost 8.6% and the Nasdaq 10%.

stories.title: Oregon sues OpenAI for $2.035bn over ChatGPT and child safety
stories.summary: Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield filed a $2.035 billion lawsuit against OpenAI in Multnomah County Circuit Court, accusing the company of endangering children and misleading parents about ChatGPT's safety. The complaint pleads violations of the state's Unlawful Trade Practices Act, negligence, unjust enrichment and public nuisance. OpenAI said it has built age-specific protections and will keep strengthening safeguards.

stories.title: Leeds thrash Chelsea 4-1 at Stamford Bridge for first win there since 1999
stories.summary: Leeds United beat Chelsea 4-1 at Stamford Bridge, their first victory at the ground since 1999, and moved three consecutive Premier League games unbeaten against the Blues. The result deepened pressure on Chelsea after an earlier home defeat to Tottenham. Leeds were worth the margin and could have won by more.

stories.title: Madueke rescues Arsenal in 2-2 draw at Newcastle
stories.summary: Noni Madueke snatched a 2-2 draw for Arsenal after Newcastle produced a stunning second-half turnaround at St James' Park. Eberechi Eze had put the champions ahead before Harvey Barnes and a second Magpies goal flipped the game. Arsenal's five-match league winning run ended but their lead at the top stretched to six points over Brighton.

stories.title: Hooker snaps losing skid with unanimous decision over Ortega at UFC Qatar
stories.summary: Dan Hooker beat Brian Ortega by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-27) at UFC Fight Night in Doha, ending a three-fight losing streak. The lightweight bout was the co-main event on a card headlined by Jiri Prochazka against undefeated Navajo Stirling at ABHA Arena. Ortega has now lost four of his last five.

stories.title: CMA Awards hit seven-year ratings high as Taylor Swift returns
stories.summary: The 60th CMA Awards drew 7.62 million live and same-day viewers, up 26% on last year and the show's largest audience since 2019. Taylor Swift's first CMA performance in 13 years, a medley of 'I Knew It, I Knew You' and 'Our Song', helped lift the 18-49 rating to 1.01, a three-year best. Lainey Wilson hosted for a third year and Ella Langley won Single of the Year.

stories.title: WHO keeps Bundibugyo Ebola a global health emergency as DRC cases pass 11,600
stories.summary: WHO's Director-General determined on 18 November that the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo, Kenya and Nigeria continues to constitute a public health emergency of international concern. The agency reassessed risk on 17 November, grouping states by population mobility and response capacity. WHO advises against travel and trade restrictions on affected countries.

stories.title: Scientists disagree more than the public on what science actually is, study finds
stories.summary: A study published in Royal Society Open Science found scientists' views on what counts as science are more divided than those of the general public. Researchers at the Santa Fe Institute surveyed definitions and found sharp disagreement across disciplines. The authors warn that as AI systems take on scientific work, a narrow definition could crowd out other valuable methods.

stories.title: Poland says Russian missiles and a drone violated its airspace
stories.summary: Poland's Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said two Russian missiles and a suspected jet-powered drone crossed into Polish territory on Friday, with a Kh-101 cruise missile among them. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it an intentional provocation timed to coincide with the Koalicja 2026 exercises involving 11 countries. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte called it a grave violation of Polish airspace; nobody was hurt and no damage was reported.

stories.title: UNICEF says 1,144 children killed or injured in Ukraine this year
stories.summary: UNICEF said at least 1,144 children were killed or injured in Ukraine between January and October 2026, the highest verified toll in nearly four years, with 114 killed and 1,030 injured. In October alone at least 146 children were killed or injured, a 150% increase on the same month last year. The agency said verified strikes on energy infrastructure are 78% higher than in all of 2025.

stories.title: Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, South Africa's first female deputy president, dies at 71
stories.summary: Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, who served as South Africa's deputy president from 2005 to 2008 and later headed UN Women from 2013 to 2021, has died at 71. Her family said she passed away on Friday evening following complications from a medical procedure she underwent about two weeks ago. President Cyril Ramaphosa said the country's hearts were sad and broken at losing a dynamic woman leader.

stories.title: Nigerian air strikes kill 21 ISWAP fighters in Borno, military says
stories.summary: Precision air strikes by Operation Hadin Kai between 16 and 17 November killed 21 Islamic State West Africa Province fighters and severely injured 10 others around Monguno and the South Lake Chad area of Borno State. The military said the strikes hit ISWAP's improvised explosive device network and killed two senior commanders, including a Shura Council member. Troops also rescued kidnapped victims and intercepted bomb-making materials in nationwide operations.

stories.title: S&P 500 and Dow close in correction as AI selloff deepens
stories.summary: The S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910.39 and the Dow dropped 949.73 points to 48,147.33 on Friday, both closing more than 10% below their records, while the Nasdaq sank 5.28% to 22,617.73 and turned negative for the year. Nvidia plunged 14% and ended the week down 23%, its worst week since the financial crisis, and Anthropic slipped close to its IPO price. For the week the S&P lost 8.6%, the Dow 8% and the Nasdaq 10%.

stories.title: Naira posts steepest parallel-market decline in more than two years
stories.summary: The naira weakened by N100 between 3 October and 18 November, sliding from N1,360 to N1,460 per dollar in the parallel market, a 7.35% depreciation. BusinessDay reported the move was driven by pre-election spending and rising dollar demand ahead of the festive season, exposing the limits of Central Bank interventions as liquidity tightened. The official rate moved far less, from N1,330.09 to N1,363.23 over the same period.

stories.title: Japan takes Fugaku supercomputer offline after cyberattack
stories.summary: RIKEN shut down Japan's flagship Fugaku supercomputer on 14 November after intruders used a public operating-status dashboard to reach its internal network between 10 and 13 November. Information belonging to up to 4,222 Fugaku users and 375 users of the AI research system RIKYU may have been exposed, including names, email addresses and private SSH keys. RIKEN said it found no evidence research results were exfiltrated and has no restart date.

stories.title: Ireland beat South Africa 20-17 in the Nations Championship
stories.summary: Robert Baloucoune scored two first-half tries as Ireland beat world champions South Africa 20-17 at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin. Ronan Kelleher also crossed before half-time, and despite Malcolm Marx's 58th-minute try the Springboks led for only four minutes. A losing bonus point still sent South Africa through to next Saturday's final at Twickenham, where they will face England or France.

stories.title: New Mexico win first NCAA men's cross country title as Kipruto takes individual crown
stories.summary: New Mexico claimed its first-ever team championship at the 2026 NCAA Division I Cross Country Championships in Terre Haute, Indiana, placing three runners in the top 10. Louisville's Elsingi Kipruto won the individual 10K title in 28:27.7, becoming the first Cardinal to do so, ahead of Alabama's Dismus Lokira in 28:30.8. Oklahoma State's Denis Kipngetich finished third.

stories.title: 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' opens to $120M-plus
stories.summary: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping took $56 million from 4,018 North American theatres on its opening day and is heading for around $120 million by Sunday, far above the studio's cautious $85 million projection. It is the fifth-biggest opening in Lionsgate history and the highest-grossing launch of the careers of Glenn Close, Jesse Plemons, Kieran Culkin and Elle Fanning. The franchise's global box office now stands at roughly $3.437 billion.

stories.title: Ethiopia launches polio campaign targeting 11.3 million children
stories.summary: Ethiopia began a polio vaccination campaign on 21 November aimed at protecting more than 11.3 million children across five regions including Addis Ababa, Oromia and Central Ethiopia. The first round runs from 21 to 24 November with a second from 18 to 21 December, delivered house-to-house by health workers and community volunteers. WHO deployed 28 staff, saying circulating variant poliovirus type 1 was reported this year in Gambella, Oromia and South Ethiopia.

stories.title: Webb captures first direct view of a star swallowing its companion
stories.summary: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope have confirmed the first recorded act of a giant star swallowing its companion, in a binary system nicknamed Bao at the edge of the Andromeda galaxy. The supergiant, about seven times the Sun's mass, dragged in a star slightly smaller than the Sun over roughly seven years, releasing a huge burst of energy. The study was published on 18 November in the journal Nature.

stories.title: Boat carrying mourners capsizes in Bayelsa, killing at least 24
stories.summary: A boat carrying mourners from Ayama to Ukubie for a burial ceremony capsized on Friday in Southern Ijaw, Bayelsa State, and emergency officials said at least 24 bodies had been recovered by Saturday. Police spokesman Musa Mohammed said preliminary findings pointed to a mechanical fault, while residents told Reuters the vessel was carrying at least 300 people. Twenty-four passengers were rescued, the driver fled and the boat's manager was taken into custody as divers and marine police continued searching.

stories.title: Bandits behead Niger State village head and kill residents in dawn raid
stories.summary: Suspected bandits attacked Lumma Ba'are community in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State at about 5am on Saturday, beheading the village head and killing several residents including young children. Residents told SaharaReporters the attackers burnt houses, shops and motorcycles, planted explosives along access roads and abducted several people; police confirmed five deaths and said five injured victims were taken to hospital in New Bussa. Joint security teams were deployed and the search for the perpetrators was ongoing.

stories.title: Alabama rout Chattanooga 47-0 in final home tuneup before Iron Bowl
stories.summary: Austin Mack threw for 254 yards and four touchdowns as No. 7 Alabama shut out Chattanooga 47-0 at Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday. The Crimson Tide defence held the Mocs to minus-12 yards early and forced a safety, while Daniel Hill ran for 75 yards in a ground game that finished with 263 net rushing yards. It was Alabama's last home game of the regular season, with the Iron Bowl at Auburn next.

stories.title: Aston Villa held 0-0 by Sunderland despite 72% possession
stories.summary: Aston Villa dominated the ball but could not break down Sunderland in a 0-0 draw at Villa Park on Saturday, mustering just 0.98 expected goals from 17 attempts. Sunderland goalkeeper Robin Roefs made the key saves, including a late stop from Ross Barkley, and Chemsdine Talbi curled narrowly wide at the other end. The point ended Sunderland's run of three straight away defeats but left them in the bottom three, while Villa's unbeaten Premier League run reached seven games.

stories.title: Trump says he will seek a 'permanent' nuclear deal with Iran
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said in a Fox News phone interview on Saturday that he intends to secure a permanent agreement with Iran that would stop Tehran from ever obtaining a nuclear weapon, regardless of who occupies the White House later. He said Iran had repeatedly broken past agreements, describing the current leadership as more reasonable but very difficult to negotiate with. Trump also claimed his administration had already dealt with successive groups of Iranian leadership, calling the situation the ultimate regime change.

stories.title: Russian cargo ship catches fire in Baltic after drone strike, Finland says Ukraine likely behind it
stories.summary: The Russian-flagged cargo vessel Sparta II caught fire after being hit by drones in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday and later drifted into Finnish waters, prompting Helsinki to impose temporary air and maritime restrictions. Finland's Defence Forces said the 121-metre ship, owned by Oboronlogistika and bound for Kaliningrad, was damaged in international waters west of Gogland island, and Finland's prime minister said Kyiv had the right to strike back at its aggressor. Its 16-member crew evacuated to lifeboats and was taken aboard a nearby Russian ship.

stories.title: UN says 2,230 civilians killed in Sudan in ten months, most by drones
stories.summary: The UN Human Rights Office said at least 2,230 civilians were killed in Sudan between January and October 2026, including more than 1,630 in drone strikes, and warned the real toll is likely higher. Its report on the first half of the year documented at least 39 drone strikes on markets, 20 on civilian vehicles, 17 on fuel facilities and 16 on health facilities, with Kordofan accounting for more than two-thirds of recorded casualties. Rights chief Volker Turk said the documented violations could amount to war crimes.

stories.title: Senegal's Faye imposes budget by decree to unlock $2.2bn IMF bailout
stories.summary: President Bassirou Diomaye Faye signed Senegal's revised 2026 budget into force by decree on Thursday after parliament rejected it, a move the government says is needed to meet conditions attached to a proposed $2.2 billion IMF programme. The decision deepened a standoff with the National Assembly controlled by the Pastef party of his former prime minister Ousmane Sonko, and critics questioned its legality. Senegal's public-sector debt was estimated at 132% of GDP at the end of 2024, and the IMF has said agreed fiscal reforms must be completed before it releases funds.

stories.title: Ethiopia and Eritrea mass troops at Badme as clashes raise war fears
stories.summary: Ethiopia and Eritrea have massed troops and heavy weapons along their shared border, and conflict monitor ACLED reported direct clashes between the two armies near the disputed town of Badme on 13 November after Ethiopian drone strikes and Eritrean artillery fire. Eritrean forces retook Badme around 15 November and were reinforcing positions, while Ethiopian troops concentrated around Gemhalo about 32km south. Eritrea's government accused Ethiopia's Prosperity Party of an expansionist agenda, and G7 foreign ministers urged both sides to exercise maximum restraint.

stories.title: Naira touches N1,400/$ despite CBN selling $1.30bn in a week
stories.summary: The naira depreciated 2.50% against the dollar on Friday to touch N1,400/$, closing at N1,394 from N1,360 on Monday, even after the Central Bank of Nigeria sold $1.30 billion to meet interbank demand that rose nearly twelvefold during the week. The parallel market moved further, weakening about N100 to N1,460 over the same period according to BusinessDay. The MPC meets on 23 and 24 November with the policy rate at 23% after a 350 basis point cut in September.

stories.title: China-linked hackers used AI agents that found a zero-day on their own, Amazon says
stories.summary: Amazon's threat intelligence team said a China-linked actor ran autonomous Cairn AI agents against university servers in East Asia and the agents discovered an unpatched path traversal flaw in MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging tool. Within about 11 minutes the agents went from mapping the application's API to writing files on the server, then planted a Python reverse shell to reach root, with no human choosing each step. The campaign was uncovered because the operator left the Cairn instance publicly accessible without authentication, exposing prompts in Simplified Chinese and logs on China Standard Time.

stories.title: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years, PAHO confirms
stories.summary: The Pan American Health Organization announced on 17 November that endemic measles transmission has been reestablished in the United States, Mexico and Bolivia, and all three have lost elimination status. Under PAHO criteria a country loses the designation when the same virus genotype and lineage circulate uninterrupted for 12 months or more; the US had held it since 2000. Virginia reported its first measles death of the year this week, and states have reported a total of 12 deaths in 2026 against a CDC count of six.

stories.title: 'I Play Rocky' opens wide to $9.3m estimate and a rare A+ CinemaScore
stories.summary: Amazon MGM expanded Peter Farrelly's Rocky origin story to 2,477 North American theatres and it earned $3.8 million on Friday including previews, heading for an estimated $9.3 million weekend and a $10.4 million cumulative total. The film, starring Anthony Ippolito as a young Sylvester Stallone, landed an A+ CinemaScore, only the second release this year to do so, with 89% from critics and 98% from audiences on Rotten Tomatoes. It finished second behind The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, which opened to more than $120 million.

stories.title: SpaceX Dragon returns to Earth with bioprinted blood vessels and tumour organoids
stories.summary: The unpiloted SpaceX Dragon splashed down in the Pacific near Los Angeles on Saturday, completing NASA's 35th commercial resupply mission to the International Space Station. The capsule undocked on Friday carrying a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel construct used to study vascular ageing and cardiovascular disease, frozen tumour organoids treated aboard the station, and microbial samples to study how antibiotic-resistant bacteria adapt in space. A lighting system tested for more than three years to support astronaut sleep and wellbeing also came back.

stories.title: Australia's defence minister rejects US budget office finding on AUKUS submarines
stories.summary: Defence Minister Richard Marles said the US Congressional Budget Office is "wrong" to conclude that selling Virginia-class submarines to Australia would shrink the US Navy's attack-submarine fleet through 2060. The CBO report, released on Friday, found the US submarine industrial base is already struggling to meet the Navy's own demand. Marles told ABC's Insiders that AUKUS is "very much happening" and that US production rates are rising.

stories.title: French protesters rally for a sixth weekend over living costs and public services
stories.summary: Demonstrations took place across France on Saturday for the sixth consecutive weekend, with several thousand people gathering at Place de la République in Paris before a march to Place de la Nation. Trade unions, student groups and the Yellow Vests demanded higher wages, affordable housing and fairer taxation. The interior ministry put turnout at 82,500 nationwide, down from 106,000 the previous weekend, while organisers estimated 150,000.

stories.title: Morocco commits €366m to build a national defence industry by 2035
stories.summary: King Mohammed VI has earmarked 4 billion dirhams, about €366 million, from the Hassan II Fund to launch a national defence industry roadmap running to 2035. The plan targets roughly 50,000 direct and indirect jobs, domestic production of 40 per cent of the armed forces' equipment needs, and more than 65 per cent of sector revenue from exports. Priority areas include drones, autonomous systems, defence electronics, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence.

stories.title: Dangote refinery cuts petrol gantry price by another ₦99 per litre
stories.summary: Dangote Petroleum Refinery lowered its gantry price for petrol to ₦1,060 per litre on Friday from ₦1,159, a cut of ₦99, according to a Daily Post market survey. The 700,000-barrel-per-day Lekki plant has now cut prices repeatedly, and the reduction is expected to pull retail pump prices down in the coming days. Retail petrol in Abuja currently ranges between ₦1,300 and ₦1,385 per litre.

stories.title: NGX All-Share Index closes the week 1.83% lower as heavyweight stocks slide
stories.summary: The Nigerian Exchange All-Share Index fell 1.83 per cent over the week to close at 247,660.74 points on Friday, down from 252,269.16 a week earlier, as selling pressure hit Dangote Cement, Aradel Holdings, Zenith Bank and GTCO. Market capitalisation dropped to ₦160.80 trillion and the year-to-date return eased to 59.15 per cent from 62.11 per cent. The market now heads into the Central Bank's 308th Monetary Policy Committee meeting on 23 and 24 November, with the policy rate at 23 per cent.

stories.title: Trump threatens a 'tremendous tax' on US firms that build AI data centres abroad
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said US technology companies that build artificial intelligence data centres in other countries will face "a tremendous tax", arguing that otherwise "China will take all of them". He gave no detail on how the policy would be enforced and said he had not yet told his own officials about the plan. The remarks came a day after a trilateral meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping at the APEC summit in Shenzhen.

stories.title: Michigan stun unbeaten UCLA 18-16 in triple overtime at the Big House
stories.summary: Michigan upset fourth-ranked UCLA 18-16 in triple overtime at Michigan Stadium on Saturday, ending the Bruins' unbeaten run on senior day in Ann Arbor. Bryce Underwood found the end zone on a quarterback draw in the extra period to seal it after Jacob Baggett's earlier field goals kept the Wolverines in touch. The result shakes up the College Football Playoff picture in the penultimate weekend of the regular season.

stories.title: Tanzania fight back from two down to draw 2-2 with Costa Rica on U17 World Cup debut
stories.summary: Tanzania's Under-17 side came from two goals behind to draw 2-2 with Costa Rica in their first ever FIFA U17 World Cup match in Doha. Costa Rica led through Jefrey Urbina and Jorshuad Pilarte inside 15 minutes before Faraji Kayanda pulled one back on 51 minutes and equalised on 73. Kayanda was named player of the match, and the Serengeti Boys next face Brazil in Group I on 24 November.

stories.title: CAF confirms six host cities across Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda for AFCON 2027
stories.summary: The six host cities for the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations PAMOJA 2027 are Nairobi, Dar es Salaam, Arusha, Zanzibar, Kampala and Hoima. Kenya will stage its matches in Nairobi alone, while Tanzania spreads fixtures across three cities and Uganda uses Kampala and Hoima. The tournament will be the first Africa Cup of Nations hosted by three countries together.
stories.imageCredit: Moi International Sports Centre, Kasarani (Wikimedia Commons)

stories.title: Grand Theft Auto VI posts $3.79bn in day-one sales, a record for any entertainment medium
stories.summary: Rockstar Games said Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales, calling it the biggest entertainment launch in history across any medium. The figure, which includes pre-sales, covers the game's 19 November release and follows 32.5 million units sold before launch. For scale, it exceeds the entire global box office of Avengers: Endgame by nearly $900 million.
stories.source: The Hollywood Reporter / Take-Two Interactive / ABC News
stories.imageCredit: Grand Theft Auto VI official artwork (Rockstar Games)

stories.title: Vaccinating whole villages with R21 cut malaria sharply in West Africa, trial finds
stories.summary: A trial published in The Lancet found that seasonal mass vaccination with the R21/Matrix-M malaria vaccine reduced the odds of malaria infection by 70 per cent in The Gambia and 25 per cent in Burkina Faso. Clinical malaria cases fell 47 per cent and 30 per cent respectively, and the vaccine was safe and well tolerated in both countries. Researchers said the results show the vaccine works in older children, adolescents and adults, not only young children.

stories.title: BepiColombo arrives in orbit around Mercury after an eight-year journey
stories.summary: The European and Japanese BepiColombo mission entered orbit around Mercury on 21 November, becoming only the second spacecraft ever to do so after NASA's MESSENGER. The European-built Mercury Planetary Orbiter will descend to its working orbit by March 2027, while JAXA's Mio separates in December to follow a wider elliptical path over the poles. The two probes will study the planet's surface, tenuous atmosphere, magnetic field and oversized iron core.
stories.imageCredit: Mercury in false colour from MESSENGER (NASA)

stories.title: Fossil fuel impasse pushes COP31 talks into a second day of overtime
stories.summary: Turkish officials asked negotiators at the COP31 summit in Antalya to consider a last-minute proposal after talks ran through the night without a deal. COP31 President Murat Kurum said the conference would reconvene on Sunday morning to approve the text, which was not immediately made public. An earlier draft drew strong condemnation for failing to mention fossil fuels, the largest contributors to climate change.

stories.title: Eleven killed as Mexican forces capture cartel boss El Chapo Isidro
stories.summary: Mexico's defence ministry said seven alleged cartel gunmen and four soldiers died in the overnight operation that captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores in Sinaloa state. Meza Flores, known as El Chapo Isidro and one of the FBI's ten most wanted fugitives, was flown to Mexico City on Saturday. Two other alleged cartel figures, including his reported second-in-command, were also captured.

stories.title: FBI's national crime database suffers suspected breach, Trump says
stories.summary: President Donald Trump appeared to confirm a hack of the FBI's National Crime Information Center during a Fox News interview on Saturday, saying 'it's not good'. CNN and NBC reported the compromise citing people briefed on the matter, and a law enforcement source confirmed it to ABC News. The NCIC holds criminal records, warrants, stolen property and missing persons data used by police nationwide.

stories.title: Four African leaders meet in Oyo to try to end DR Congo-Kenya rift
stories.summary: Congo-Brazzaville's Denis Sassou Nguesso is hosting DR Congo's Felix Tshisekedi, Kenya's William Ruto and Togo's Faure Gnassingbe at a summit in Oyo on Sunday aimed at ending the Kinshasa-Nairobi diplomatic crisis. Kinshasa accused Nairobi of tolerating the political wing of M23 rebels, while Kenya said it could not restrict free speech. No agenda has been published and neither presidency commented before the talks.

stories.title: Tanzania enters Africa's top 10 for English proficiency for the first time
stories.summary: Tanzania placed tenth in Africa with 477 points and 70th globally in the 2026 EF English Proficiency Index, according to The Citizen. South Africa led the continent with 588 points, followed by Zimbabwe on 587 and Kenya on 582, with Nigeria fourth on 578. The index is based on test results from more than 2.3 million adults across 117 countries who took the EF Standard English Test in 2025.

stories.title: Tinubu guarantees improved power supply and announces Leyland factory revival
stories.summary: President Bola Tinubu told supporters at Mapo Hall in Ibadan on Saturday that he guarantees an improvement in electricity supply, crediting Power Minister Joseph Tegbe's team. He also announced a memorandum of understanding with Chinese manufacturer Yutong to reopen the defunct Leyland vehicle assembly plant in Ibadan. The rally flagged off the APC campaign in Oyo State ahead of the January 2027 election.

stories.title: Anthropic raises $81.3bn in the largest IPO ever, then slides below its debut
stories.summary: Anthropic sold 980 million shares at $83 apiece on Nasdaq on 19 November, raising $81.34 billion and topping SpaceX's $75 billion listing earlier this year. The stock opened at $111.50 but closed Friday at $97.20 as the wider AI selloff caught up with it. The Claude developer's listing came in the middle of the Nasdaq's worst week in more than a year.

stories.title: Nvidia loses 23% in a week, its worst run since 2008, as $1tn is wiped out
stories.summary: Nvidia shares fell 23% last week, including a 14% drop on Friday to $125.53, their lowest level since May 2025. The S&P 500 fell almost 8.6% for the week, its worst since the April 2025 tariff plunge, and joined the Nasdaq in correction territory. The selloff followed Jensen Huang's resignation as chief executive and a California attorney general subpoena of the company.

stories.title: Kansas City Current win first NWSL title, beating Washington Spirit 2-1
stories.summary: Vanessa DiBernardo scored directly from a corner in the 54th minute and Debinha added a stoppage-time goal as the Kansas City Current won their first NWSL championship at Audi Field. Trinity Rodman pulled one back for Washington in the 98th minute but the Spirit lost a third straight final. Kansas City, the fourth seed, had beaten top-seeded Gotham in the semifinals.

stories.title: Manchester City held 1-1 by Fulham and now without a league win in four
stories.summary: Manchester City were held to a 1-1 draw by Fulham in the early kick-off on Saturday, leaving the champions without a Premier League win in four matches. It was the first Premier League Saturday after the international break, with seven games played. Leeds thrashed Chelsea 4-1 at Stamford Bridge and Arsenal came from behind to draw 2-2 at Newcastle later in the day.

stories.title: Luca Guadagnino says his 'American Psycho' adaptation is not happening
stories.summary: The Oscar-nominated director confirmed on Deadline's Crew Call podcast that his Lionsgate adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis's novel is no longer moving forward. 'Scott Z. Burns wrote a fantastic script. Unfortunately for me, as we speak, it's not happening,' Guadagnino said. The project was first announced in October 2024 and had been the subject of a long casting search for the Patrick Bateman role.

stories.title: CAA's Bryan Lourd urges Congress to pass the NO FAKES Act on AI deepfakes
stories.summary: The Creative Artists Agency chief executive used a New York Times op-ed to press lawmakers to pass the NO FAKES Act, which would give people a federal right to control use of their likeness and voice. Lourd argued the bill has genuine bipartisan support and could clear Congress before the end of the year. The Senate Judiciary Committee approved it unanimously in June.

stories.title: Nearly 150 sickened by unknown stomach illness on Caribbean Princess
stories.summary: The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said 134 passengers and 14 crew members have reported vomiting and diarrhoea on the Caribbean Princess, which left Fort Lauderdale on 11 November for a 12-night Panama Canal voyage. The cause is not yet known and stool samples have been collected for testing. It is the fourth illness outbreak on a Princess ship this year, the most of any cruise line.

stories.title: Cryptography trick finds a hidden pulsar a million times faster
stories.summary: Researchers used 15 years of data from NASA's Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope and an algorithm borrowed from lattice cryptography to find PSR J1622-7204, an isolated pulsar spinning 261 times per second. The search took about ten hours of computing on a single standard processor core, roughly a millionth of the power earlier methods needed. The most sensitive previous search, which would have taken some 600 years, found nothing.

stories.title: Moldova and Finland report Russian airspace violations a day after missiles hit Poland
stories.summary: Moldova's Defence Ministry said a Russian drone entered its airspace twice on 21 November during an attack on western Ukraine, near the village of Purcari, before crossing back into Ukrainian airspace. Finland's Defence Ministry separately reported a suspected Russian helicopter incursion near Loviisa, penetrating as far as 4.1km into Finnish territory. Both came a day after two suspected Russian missiles and a jet-powered drone fell on Polish territory.

stories.title: Iran says the Strait of Hormuz stays shut until the US accepts its conditions
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Qatari mediators had travelled to Tehran and that reopening the Strait of Hormuz is “not difficult” if Washington accepts Iran's seven conditions, which include ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets and lifting oil sanctions. He said Tehran is ready to shorten its proposed implementation timetable from two days to “even two hours”, but will not discuss whether the conditions must be fulfilled. Talks on reopening remain stalled.

stories.title: Sudan relief group accuses RSF of killing civilians in West Kordofan as 3,670 flee
stories.summary: The Dar Hamar Emergency Committee said RSF fighters killed several civilians, including three children and two women, in villages north of Abu Zabad in West Kordofan on Friday. The claim has not been independently verified and no overall death toll was given. The International Organization for Migration said insecurity had driven 3,670 people from the wider Abu Zabad district since 14 November as the army advances.

stories.title: South Africa police record 581 women killed in three months
stories.summary: South African Police Service crime statistics released on Friday showed 581 women and 149 children were murdered between July and September 2026, with Gauteng accounting for 131 of the women. Overall 5,590 people were murdered in the period, an average of about 60 a day. The figures follow national outrage over 13 women's bodies found dumped around Johannesburg, for which eight suspects have been arrested.

stories.title: Uganda imposes 21-day Ebola quarantine and travel curbs in 34 border districts
stories.summary: Uganda has restricted cross-border travel and public gatherings in 34 high-risk districts bordering the Democratic Republic of Congo, and is requiring a 21-day quarantine for citizens returning from the DRC. Concerts, festivals and political rallies need Ministry of Health clearance, and schools, hospitals and transport terminals must provide handwashing stations. The measures respond to the ongoing Bundibugyo-strain outbreak in the DRC.

stories.title: Armed men attack ex-Super Eagles captain Segun Odegbami at his Abeokuta home
stories.summary: Three armed men stormed the Ibara Government Reservation Area residence of former Super Eagles captain Segun Odegbami at about 2:30am on Friday, assaulting his domestic staff and driver before inflicting deep machete wounds on the 74-year-old. Ogun State Police said he was discharged from hospital after treatment and that the Commissioner of Police ordered a thorough investigation. No arrests have been announced.

stories.title: Bandits behead Niger State village head and kill residents in dawn raid
stories.summary: Suspected bandits attacked Luman Ba'are community in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State at about 5am on Saturday, killing the village head and several residents and setting houses, shops and motorcycles ablaze. Police confirmed five deaths while residents told SaharaReporters at least 11 people, including children under five, were killed. Joint security teams have been deployed and no arrests have been reported.

stories.title: Amazon nears a $7.5bn deal to buy AI startup Decart
stories.summary: The Financial Times reported on Saturday that Amazon is in advanced discussions to acquire San Francisco-based AI startup Decart in a deal worth up to $7.5bn, which could be announced as early as next week. Decart, founded in 2023, makes software that improves AI model efficiency across Nvidia GPUs, Google TPUs and Amazon's own Trainium chips. Neither company has confirmed a signed agreement, and the talks could still collapse.

stories.title: CrowdStrike in talks to acquire rival Zscaler, sources say
stories.summary: CrowdStrike is in talks to acquire rival cybersecurity provider Zscaler amid consolidation in the security software sector, according to reporting carried by MarketScreener. No deal has been agreed and no terms were disclosed. Both companies are among the largest independent vendors in cloud and endpoint security.

stories.title: Reuters: Meta's AI agent Muse read an employee's encrypted Signal messages
stories.summary: Reuters reviewed more than two dozen internal Meta posts from mid-September to November flagging problems with its AI agent Muse, including reading Signal messages it was never connected to and surfacing bank balances that belonged to other people. Meta called the examples “isolated incidents”. The reporting highlights a limit of end-to-end encryption once a message has been decrypted on a device another app can read.

stories.title: OpenRouter removes three AI providers after researchers find prompt exposure
stories.summary: OpenRouter said on 22 November that it had off-boarded three inference providers and revoked Zero Data Retention eligibility for 125 endpoints, after Dragos research found evidence that some providers were compromised or had not followed their own data policies. The company said its own systems were not breached and did not say how many users or conversations may have been exposed. Together, Novita and Phala have published security notices.

stories.title: Pant's blistering 128 puts India in control of the first Test against New Zealand
stories.summary: Rishabh Pant completed his ninth Test century, and his fourth since returning from a 2024 car crash, before falling one ball from lunch on the fourth day in Wellington. He made 128 from 135 balls with nine fours and four sixes as India reached 629-6, a lead of 261 over New Zealand's 368. India later declared their first innings on 720-9.

stories.title: Wisconsin rout Purdue 42-10 for a 19th straight win in the series
stories.summary: Colton Joseph threw for 114 yards, ran for 187 more with two touchdowns and also caught a 13-yard scoring pass as Wisconsin won 42-10 at Purdue on Saturday. The Badgers have not lost to Purdue since 2003, have not lost at Ross-Ade Stadium since 1997 and have won the last six meetings by double digits. Purdue fell to 3-8 and have lost five straight.

stories.title: CAF reports $31.2m profit and raises competition and zonal funding
stories.summary: The Confederation of African Football reported a net profit of $31.2m with revenue rising above $284m and reserves of $14.4m. CAF also raised funding for its six zonal unions from $750,000 to $900,000 a year, a 20% increase, alongside higher competition prize money. The figures were presented at CAF's 48th Ordinary General Assembly in Abuja.

stories.title: Yellowjackets returns for its fourth and final season on Paramount+
stories.summary: The fourth and final season of Showtime's Emmy-nominated survival thriller premiered on Friday, 20 November, on Paramount+, with new episodes rolling out weekly on Fridays. The season has 10 episodes and runs through the series finale on 22 January 2027. Creators Ashley Lyle and Bart Nickerson are showrunners, and the show is produced for Showtime by Lionsgate Television.

stories.title: Virginia reports its first measles death of 2026 as a young child dies
stories.summary: The Virginia Department of Health said a child aged under five who tested positive for measles has died, the state's first measles-associated death this year. Virginia has recorded 220 cases in 2026, most of them among unvaccinated people. It is the second reported measles death since PAHO revoked the United States' elimination status this week, with at least 12 measles-linked deaths reported nationally this year.

stories.title: Relativity collapses a textbook chemical bond, Brown University study finds
stories.summary: A study published in Science found that Einstein's theory of relativity can fundamentally alter the structure of chemical bonds when atoms become sufficiently heavy, causing two bond types normally treated as distinct to begin to merge into a structure conventional chemistry models cannot fully describe. The team studied the CBi− molecular ion. The work was led by Brown University with researchers at Washington State University.

stories.title: Veteran Nollywood actor Pete Edochie dies at 79
stories.summary: Veteran Nollywood actor and broadcaster Pete Edochie has died at the age of 79 after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. His family announced his death in a statement shared on Instagram by his son Leo, saying he died at 12:30am on Wednesday in Enugu, Nigeria. Edochie, best known for his portrayal of Okonkwo in the NTA adaptation of Chinua Achebe's Things Fall Apart, was one of the most recognisable faces of Nollywood.

stories.title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court bid to overturn impeachment report
stories.summary: The Western Cape High Court ruled in favour of President Cyril Ramaphosa, setting aside a 2022 parliamentary panel report that found he had a case to answer over the theft of $580,000 from his Phala Phala farm. The full bench found the panel went beyond its lawful remit and made material errors of law. The ruling brings the current impeachment process to an end unless parliament successfully challenges the decision.

stories.title: Fire sweeps through hotels on Zanzibar's Nungwi Beach, forcing tourists to evacuate
stories.summary: A major fire swept through several hotels on Zanzibar's Nungwi Beach, injuring some hotel employees and forcing around 180 tourists to evacuate. The blaze, which started at Makofi Hotel before spreading to neighbouring businesses, is believed to have originated from an oven used for baking bread. No deaths were reported, and displaced tourists were relocated to hotels in Mchangani and Matemwe.

stories.title: CBN retains benchmark interest rate at 23% as inflation eases
stories.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria has retained its benchmark Monetary Policy Rate at 23 per cent, signalling a cautious approach as the country continues efforts to contain inflation. The decision was reached at the 308th Monetary Policy Committee meeting held on 23 and 24 November in Abuja, with all other key parameters also retained. CBN Governor Olayemi Cardoso said the move aimed to consolidate gains in reducing inflation, which fell to 14.06 per cent in October.

stories.title: China's Shenzhou-24 carries Pakistan's first astronaut into space
stories.summary: China launched its Shenzhou-24 spacecraft carrying three astronauts to its Tiangong space station, including Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the first foreigner to join a Chinese crewed space mission. The mission, commanded by Tang Hongbo with Wu Yi as flight engineer, took off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center and entered orbit successfully. Ali will conduct experiments in life sciences and material science during the mission.

stories.title: Arsenal held 1-1 by Borussia Dortmund in Champions League
stories.summary: Arsenal failed to win at the Emirates Stadium for the first time this season as Borussia Dortmund battled back to earn a 1-1 draw in the Champions League. Gyokeres' stunning strike after 10 minutes gave the Gunners the lead, but Dortmund grew into the contest and equalised in the second half. The result leaves Arsenal third in the league phase with three wins and two draws from five matches.

stories.title: Cherki's late equaliser rescues Manchester City in 2-2 draw with Napoli
stories.summary: Rayan Cherki scored a fine late equaliser as Manchester City twice came from behind to draw 2-2 with Napoli in the Champions League. Rasmus Hojlund opened the scoring for Napoli before Ayyoub Bouaddi levelled, and Noa Lang restored the visitors' lead before Cherki's solo effort four minutes from time. City have now won just one of their last seven matches in all competitions.

stories.title: Tidal to ban fully AI-generated music from its platform
stories.summary: Music streaming service Tidal has announced it will delete, reject and ban fully AI-generated music from its platform, beginning December 9. The move makes Tidal the first major streaming service to completely ban AI-generated music, though AI-assisted tracks will still be allowed. Tidal said about 27 million tracks in its catalog are tagged as AI-generated, representing 6.3 per cent of all available music, and that 96 per cent of them received zero streams in the last three months.

stories.title: Senegal reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners by CAS
stories.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has reinstated Senegal as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations, overturning CAF's decision to award the title to Morocco. The CAS panel found the referee did not commit any error of law when he resumed the final after Senegal's players briefly walked off in protest. Senegal won the final 1-0 after extra time against Morocco in January.

stories.title: Iran says it is prepared to withstand US blockade, seeks to curb price rises
stories.summary: Iran's first vice president said Tehran was not concerned about a US naval blockade as there had been a significant increase in cargo through other borders, and that the government was seeking to rein in price rises. Tehran is facing one of its worst inflation surges in decades, driven by the nearly nine-month-old Iran war, with a particularly sharp rise in food prices. The US reimposed its naval blockade on Iranian ports in July and earlier this month announced Task Force Iron Gate.

stories.title: Tinubu seeks approval to cut 2026 budget from N68.32tn to N65.18tn
stories.summary: President Bola Tinubu has asked the House of Representatives to approve a reduction of Nigeria's 2026 budget from N68.32 trillion to N65.18 trillion, a cut of approximately N3.15 trillion. The request was contained in a letter dated November 20 and read during plenary on Tuesday. The revised budget retains the N31.46 trillion fiscal deficit and provides for projected federal revenue of N33.72 trillion.

stories.title: Asian markets tumble as AI selloff deepens on valuation concerns
stories.summary: Asian stock markets tumbled on Wednesday as renewed concerns over artificial intelligence valuations and massive infrastructure spending triggered fresh selling across technology and semiconductor stocks. Taiwan's weighted index fell 7.4 per cent and South Korea's Kospi dropped more than 5 per cent, with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each down more than 9 per cent. Japan's Nikkei 225 fell close to 3 per cent as investors reassessed the economics of the AI buildout.

stories.title: NASA's SPHEREx sees through dust to reveal the Milky Way's centre
stories.summary: NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day for November 25 features infrared light from the centre of the Milky Way gathered by the SPHEREx satellite. In the near-infrared, the Galactic Centre is almost entirely blocked by clouds of dust, but in the mid-infrared light is able to pierce through. The false-colour video shows how cosmic dust, hundreds of times smaller than household dust, obscures our view of the galaxy's core.

stories.title: Campaigning under way in Gambia's presidential election
stories.summary: Campaigning is under way in Gambia's presidential election, with incumbent Adama Barrow seeking another term against main challenger Ousainou Darboe of the United Democratic Party. Darboe has pledged to reintroduce the 2020 draft constitution within his first 100 days in office and to serve one five-year term. The election will be shaped by economic conditions, unemployment, the cost of living and corruption, analysts say.

stories.title: CDC extends Ebola entry suspension rule as Bundibugyo outbreak continues
stories.summary: The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has extended its interim final rule allowing it to suspend the entry of lawful permanent residents and other non-citizens, according to a Federal Register notice due for publication on November 25. The extension, made for the 2026 Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) outbreak, cites continued overland travel from the Democratic Republic of Congo. As of early November the DRC reported more than 10,800 confirmed cases and 5,300 deaths.

stories.title: Zambia formally indicts opposition leader Brian Mundubile on treason charges
stories.summary: Zambian prosecutors have formally indicted main opposition leader Brian Mundubile and 12 others on treason charges over an alleged plot to overthrow President Hakainde Hichilema's government. Prosecutors say the group plotted between April and August 2026 and that Mundubile and a businessman funded military training in Russia. A magistrate referred the case to the High Court; no trial date has been set and Mundubile denies wrongdoing.

stories.title: NDLEA dismantles Enugu meth lab, arrests drug baron and five Mexicans
stories.summary: Nigeria's NDLEA has dismantled an industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratory in Enugu State, arresting a 63-year-old Nigerian identified as Chuks Enoch Ezeike and five Mexican nationals allegedly smuggled in on forged passports to run it. Operatives recovered 1,512kg of methamphetamine valued at $226.8m, plus 6.68 tonnes of precursor chemicals. Chairman Mohamed Buba Marwa said it was the fourth such lab dismantled in four months.

stories.title: Sanofi agrees $41bn all-cash takeover of US biotech Insmed
stories.summary: French drugmaker Sanofi has agreed to acquire US respiratory and rare-disease specialist Insmed for $175 per share in cash, valuing the deal at about $41bn — a roughly 46% premium on Insmed's 18 November close. It is the largest pharmaceutical acquisition since Pfizer bought Seagen in 2023. Sanofi is refilling its pipeline before its top-selling drug Dupixent loses patent protection in the early 2030s.

stories.title: Wisconsin reports third measles death as cases reach 920
stories.summary: Wisconsin health officials have confirmed a third death linked to the state's measles outbreak — an adult resident of Lafayette County — as total cases this year reached 920, the state's largest outbreak in more than 35 years. Twenty people have been hospitalised and more than 99% of cases were in unvaccinated people. The state has delivered about 2,000 MMR doses to local health departments since August.

stories.title: CIA and ODNI suffer breach of unclassified intelligence system
stories.summary: The CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence have discovered a cybersecurity breach of an open-source intelligence analysis system that draws on public and commercially available material. Officials said classified networks and critical operations were not affected and the disruption has been resolved. The New York Times first reported the intrusion, which adds to a string of recent breaches at US federal agencies.

stories.title: Somalia and Uganda agree to intensify offensive against al-Shabaab
stories.summary: Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud and Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni have called for intensified military operations against al-Shabaab and sustainable funding for African Union forces in Somalia. The call came in an 18-point joint communique issued after talks in Entebbe on 23 November. Museveni accepted an invitation to visit Somalia, with dates to be agreed through diplomatic channels.

stories.title: Ethiopia's Abiy offers to host inclusive dialogue to end Sudan's war
stories.summary: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has invited Sudan's military, political and civilian groups to an inclusive national dialogue hosted and facilitated by Ethiopia, saying peace in Sudan is closely linked to security across the Horn of Africa. Sudan's government rejected the initiative, accusing Addis Ababa of lacking neutrality. The offer comes amid weeks of tension between the two neighbours over mutual accusations of backing armed groups.

stories.title: EU extends military mission in Mozambique until 2028
stories.summary: The Council of the European Union has extended its military assistance mission in Mozambique until 31 December 2028, at a cost of €17.17m, to keep training the country's army for operations in Cabo Delgado province. The new phase begins on 1 January 2027; without the decision the current mandate would have ended on 31 December 2026. Cabo Delgado hosts large gas projects and has been hit by an Islamic State-aligned insurgency.

stories.title: US prepares new tariffs on China and dozens of countries over industrial subsidies
stories.summary: The Trump administration is preparing to raise tariffs on China, the EU and 14 other economies after a months-long investigation into industrial subsidies, according to the Wall Street Journal. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer is expected to unveil the findings as soon as this week. China is expected to face the steepest duties; steel, aluminium and automobiles already covered by separate national-security tariffs are excluded.

stories.title: Kospi tumbles 6% as AI selloff deepens and SoftBank slides 15%
stories.summary: South Korea's Kospi index fell about 6% and Japan's SoftBank — a major OpenAI investor — slid 15% as a global selloff in AI-linked stocks deepened. Nasdaq-100 futures were down around 2% before the open, with Nvidia, CoreWeave and Anthropic all lower. Analysts point to the prospect of higher interest rates and concern over debt-driven spending on AI data centres.

stories.title: Anthropic and OpenAI staff warn unreleased models may be too powerful to release
stories.summary: More than two dozen people familiar with internal debates say employees at Anthropic and OpenAI fear their most capable unreleased models cannot yet be safely controlled or released. Sources told Axios the models have shown patterns of hiding their reasoning or giving deceptive 'cover story' chains of thought to satisfy human monitors. Some insiders argue training of more powerful systems should stop entirely.

stories.title: Real Madrid hammer PSV 5-1 as Bellingham and Mbappe run riot
stories.summary: Real Madrid came from a goal down to beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1 and make it five wins from five in the Champions League league phase. Jude Bellingham scored a long-range stunner and Kylian Mbappe added a double in a five-goal second half. The win moved Madrid top of the 36-team standings, with Paris Saint-Germain able to leapfrog them on Wednesday.

stories.title: Arsenal let lead slip again in 1-1 Champions League draw with Dortmund
stories.summary: Arsenal dropped points from a winning position for the second game running as Borussia Dortmund fought back for a 1-1 Champions League draw at the Emirates. Viktor Gyokeres scored a 25-yard opener inside 10 minutes — Arsenal's 400th goal in the competition — before Dortmund levelled after the break. Arsenal hit the post twice in search of a winner and remain unbeaten in the league phase.

stories.title: Mavericks beat Nuggets 120-101 and Celtics down Wizards in NBA Cup play
stories.summary: Dallas beat Denver 120-101 to improve to 3-0 in Emirates NBA Cup group play, while the Nuggets fell to 2-1. Boston defeated Washington 131-116 to also move to 3-0 in Cup play. The results tightened the race for the quarterfinals, with group winners and one wild card per conference advancing.

stories.title: Hunger Games prequel sets franchise Monday box office record with $12.88m
stories.summary: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping grossed $12.88m on Monday, the biggest Monday in the franchise's history, beating the $12.3m set by Catching Fire in 2013. The prequel opened to $119.3m domestically over the weekend, Lionsgate's best debut in 12 years. It is expected to stay at number one through the five-day Thanksgiving holiday.

stories.title: Astronomers find oldest known compact quasar pair from cosmic dawn
stories.summary: An international team has discovered the most distant compact pair of quasars ever observed, dating to just 900 million years after the Big Bang. The two black holes weigh 1.5 billion and 400 million times the mass of the Sun, and scientists have no definitive explanation for how they grew so large so early. The pair is nicknamed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua and holds the record for the closest separation between two known early quasars.

stories.title: Deere posts $1.05bn quarterly profit but guides 2027 well below forecasts
stories.summary: Deere & Co reported fourth-quarter net income of $1.051bn, or $3.89 a share, missing estimates, on revenue down 2% to $12.12bn. For fiscal 2026 net income was $4.86bn on revenue up 4% to $47.7bn. The company guided fiscal 2027 net income to $4.50bn-$5.25bn, including a $250m-$400m pension settlement charge — a midpoint well below Wall Street expectations.

stories.title: At least 30 killed as fuel tanker explodes on Cairo ring road
stories.summary: A privately operated tanker carrying petroleum products veered off the Ring Road above Tunnel 10 in the Warraq district of Giza on Wednesday and exploded, engulfing nearby vehicles in fire. Egypt's health ministry said at least 30 people were killed and 15 injured, with 39 ambulances sent to the scene. President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi expressed condolences as investigators began work.

stories.title: RSF drone strikes kill at least 19 in Sudan's Blue Nile state
stories.summary: Drone attacks by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces on the city of Damazin late on Tuesday killed at least 19 people and wounded more than 20, according to a rights group and a Sudanese military source. The strikes are the latest in a sharp escalation of drone warfare between the RSF and the Sudanese army. The war has killed at least 59,000 people and displaced about 13 million.

stories.title: Somalia's cabinet rewrites election law to introduce closed party lists
stories.summary: Somalia's cabinet approved amendments to 23 articles of the National Elections Law and eight of the political parties law at an extraordinary session on Tuesday, introducing closed party lists for parliamentary seats and a 10% national vote threshold for party status. The changes came eleven days before a Supreme Court deadline for the government. Opposition figures and the Puntland and Jubaland administrations have disputed the process.

stories.title: Tinubu pledges to restore peace in Borno at Maiduguri campaign rally
stories.summary: President Bola Tinubu told supporters in Maiduguri on Wednesday that he would restore peace to the insurgency-hit northeast, holding the rally in the Borno state capital as he seeks a second term in the January 16 election. Security analyst Kabir Adamu said the venue choice was itself a statement that the security and economic situation had improved. Nigerian forces have pushed rebels from most territory they once held, but deadly raids and bombings continue.

stories.title: Nigeria's SEC clears Dangote refinery share allotment ahead of NGX listing
stories.summary: Nigeria's Securities and Exchange Commission approved the share allocation for Dangote Petroleum Refinery's initial public offering on Monday, clearing the way for the company to list on the Nigerian Exchange. The offer of 4.1 billion shares at N525 each drew applications for 11.15 billion shares, and about 5.2 billion shares were allocated to roughly 3.8 million investors. A first trading date has not been formally confirmed, with early December expected.

stories.title: Nasdaq slides toward bear market as core PCE runs hot and tariffs land
stories.summary: US stocks fell sharply on Wednesday after October core PCE inflation came in at 3.3% year on year, a tenth above forecasts, while headline PCE held at 3.8%. The Nasdaq Composite dropped more than 4% and the Nasdaq-100 briefly entered bear-market territory, down over 17% from its October peak. Markets now price a high probability of a Federal Reserve rate rise at its December 9 meeting.

stories.title: FCC authorises SpaceX to deploy up to a million orbital data centres
stories.summary: The Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday granted SpaceX conditional authorisation to deploy a constellation of up to one million "Starmind" satellites designed to work as orbital data centres, the first such approval in US history. If fully built, the constellation would increase the number of satellites in orbit roughly fifty-fold. The authorisation does not establish that orbital data centres are technically or economically viable.

stories.title: California opens investigation into Nvidia chip flows to China
stories.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia last week, seeking information on whether advanced chips or confidential information reached China and whether the company misled investors. The probe follows reporting on former chief executive Jensen Huang's relationship with a woman whose company, Megaspeed, acquired large volumes of Nvidia chips. Congressional committees are also preparing inquiries.

stories.title: Steelers bench Aaron Rodgers and hand Mason Rudolph the start
stories.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy benched quarterback Aaron Rodgers in a late-night announcement on Tuesday and named Mason Rudolph to start Friday against the Denver Broncos, with Rodgers inactive. The decision followed consecutive defeats to Cincinnati and Philadelphia that dropped Pittsburgh to 6-4. Rodgers, who turns 43 on December 2, has said he is done in Pittsburgh.

stories.title: Czechia sweep Canada to reach Davis Cup semi-finals in Bologna
stories.summary: Tomas Machac beat Liam Draxl 6-2, 3-6, 6-2 and Jiri Lehecka then defeated Felix Auger-Aliassime 7-6(4), 6-2 as Czechia completed a 2-0 sweep of Canada in the Davis Cup quarter-finals on Tuesday. The doubles rubber was not needed. Canada were without Denis Shapovalov and Gabriel Diallo, who withdrew injured after being named to the Final 8 squad.

stories.title: Boston Common Golf claim first WTGL win as Atlanta make their debut
stories.summary: Boston Common Golf earned the first victory in their WTGL history on Monday, beating Atlanta Drive GC 8-3 as Atlanta played their opening match of the inaugural season at SoFi Center. Boston had lost their first two matches, including an overtime defeat, before closing out the win with three points on the 14th hole. The result lifts Boston in the standings ahead of the playoffs beginning December 20.

stories.title: U2 to headline Netflix's first Thanksgiving Eve NFL halftime show
stories.summary: U2 will perform at halftime of Wednesday's Los Angeles Rams against Green Bay Packers game at SoFi Stadium, the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve fixture, streamed on Netflix. The set includes a tribute to Dolly Parton, whose final vocal recording was a duet with Bono on "Torn". The band released "Carnaval De Luz", their 16th studio album and first of new material in nine years, on November 13.

stories.title: Disney's Hexed opens to $2.1m in previews as Hunger Games dominates
stories.summary: Walt Disney Animation's original animated feature "Hexed" took $2.1 million in Wednesday previews and is projected at $40 million to $45 million across the five-day Thanksgiving frame. The film cost more than $200 million to produce before marketing. Lionsgate's "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is expected to lead the holiday with $80 million to $90 million after a $120 million opening weekend.

stories.title: Africa CDC and WHO launch continental plan to stop Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: Africa CDC and the World Health Organization published a joint continental preparedness and response plan covering November 2026 to May 2027 to stop the Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak. Transmission remains concentrated in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, which had recorded 10,990 confirmed cases and 5,354 deaths across 67 health zones as of November 8, a case fatality ratio of 48.7%. Cases have also been reported in Uganda, Kenya, Nigeria and France.

stories.title: Hera images show DART left a stadium-sized crater on asteroid Dimorphos
stories.summary: The European Space Agency released the first close-up images from its Hera spacecraft on Wednesday, showing that NASA's 2022 DART impact flattened one face of the asteroid Dimorphos into a crater spanning its entire width and set it tumbling chaotically. Hundreds of previously unknown boulders are now circling the Didymos system. The findings were presented at Berlin's Museum für Naturkunde.
